full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the opposite party Nos. 1-7 as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No. 271 of 1979 before the 1st Munsif (now Assistant Judge) Satkania, Chittagong for declaration of title and partition against the petitioner and defendant-respondent opposite parties as defendants stating, inter-alia that the schedule property originally belonged to one Ahmed Ali by virtue of a patta dated 12-6-1890 and accordingly, CS Khatian stands recorded in his name. The said Ahmed Ali died leaving two sons namely; defendant No.1 and Azizur Rahman, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and daughter, plaintiff No.2. According to law of inheritance each son got 2/5th share and the daughter got 1/5th share. During RS operation taking advantage of the minority of the heirs of CS recorded tenant i,e the claimant, Hasan Ali and others got their names recorded in RS Khatian collusively though they have/had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. On the basis of RS Khatian they having failed to enter into possession of the suit land, created some forged documents in favour of defendant Nos. 5-26. The claim of the plaintiffs in the schedule land is 1.64 acres out of 2.74 acres being 3/5th shares. The property in question has not yet been partitioned among the co-sharer. The defendants threatening the plaintiff with possession and as such, the plaintiff demanded partition of the property but the defendants refused to do so. Hence the suit. 

 8. Mr Abdul Momen Chowdhury with Mr Amulya Kumar Sarker, the learned Advocates appearing for the opposite parties submit that the property in question belonged to Ahmed Ali, predecessor of the plaintiffs who got the same by a patta dated 12-6-1890. During RS operation names of Hasan Ali and others wrongly recorded along with the names of heirs of CS recorded owner Ahmed Ali. Mr Chowdhury further submits that the trial court relying on the alleged auction purchase by the defendant No.22 and disbelieving the case of the plaintiff most illegally dismissed the suit. At the appellate stage the plaintiffs could able to collect information from the concerned record room that the story of alleged auction sale is not true and to that effect the concerned record room issued two information slips dated 22-9-1992 giving information that “সূচিপত্র থেকে দেখা যায় যে, উল্লেখিত নম্বরের কোন কর আদায়ের মোকদ্দমা অথবা জারী মোকদ্দমা সূচিপত্রে লিপিবদ্ধ নাই।” These two information slips issued by the record room show that there was no existence of Rent Suit No. 2459 of 1935 and Rent Execution Case No. 325 of 1936, in the relevant Suit Register. The opposite side also collected an information slip with an information that the record of the said suit has been destroyed. This information given by the record room has created controversy about auction sale of the suit property for which the appellate court for proper adjudication of the matter in dispute thought it necessary to send back the suit on remand for fresh trial upon taking fresh evidences from both sides and as such, the appellate court has not committed any error of law and the judgment and decree of the appellate court has not in any way prejudiced the defendant in suit and has not occasioned any failure of justice and as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.
